source.title: Tropical Cyclone Attributes in Sparse Autoencoder Features of an AI Weather Model
source.authors: Jia-Pei Liu; Rui-Dong Li; Ting Sun; Guang-Heng Ni

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports results and makes an explicit argument that cyclone information should not be identified with one fixed SAE feature: feature identities differ across independently trained SAEs while the broader organization recurs. This challenges the stable, canonical part of V5, but does not test whether SAE features are complete.
record.gate_note: The study measures cyclone-attribute relations in SAE features of GraphCast, a weather model, not an LLM or a toy network. It does not test feature interference, capacity competition, or whether features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional. Results cited from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper gives weak, indirect evidence on V5 stability, plus an explicit argument against equating information with one fixed SAE feature. Across five Layer-8 TopK SAE seeds, the leading cyclone feature's F1 (0.345–0.512) and margin (0.027–0.308) vary. In one seed, the F1 leader is not the best pressure-structure feature. It never matches features across seeds, so canonicality is argued rather than measured. Most rows (R1–R8) measure how attribute relations spread across features, not whether SAE features are stable units.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also stress their inference: event information should not be tied to one fixed SAE feature. Instead, the organization of attribute relations is the reproducible level of description. They note the analysis cannot separate physical covariation, GraphCast encoding, and SAE decomposition effects.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes GraphCast hidden states using TopK sparse autoencoders and physical-attribute readouts. It does not reproduce the toy-network method or test its superposition geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The study did not test sensitivity to SAE dictionary size, sparsity, other training choices, or the F1-selected subset size. Feature identity and rankings varied across independent SAE fits.

fits_no_version.finding: In GraphCast SAEs, each cyclone attribute (position, intensity, pressure structure) relates to multiple features. Position and pressure-structure relations overlap in a smaller subset (dictionary-wide Nshared=4.38). This organization recurs across five seeds and all 16 layers without feature alignment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Physical-attribute relations of a weather event are distributed but partially bundled across SAE features. This organization, rather than individual features, is reproducible across SAE seeds and layers.

fits_no_version.finding: In deeper layers, the fixed F1-leading feature matches cyclone position and pressure structure at t+6h better than at t. ΔF1 is positive from Layer 8 and Δρ positive from Layer 9.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE readouts in deeper GraphCast processor layers align with the forecast state rather than the current state.

record.peer_reviewed: Submitted to Geophysical Research Letters; peer-review status not stated.
record.problems: The analysis is limited to GraphCast, 2018–2019 states, and 205 cyclones. It uses correspondence readouts rather than interventions, so it does not establish that GraphCast relies on these features. The authors did not test sensitivity to SAE settings or the selected subset size, and state that their analysis cannot separate physical-attribute covariation, GraphCast encoding, and SAE decomposition effects.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. The study also reports lifecycle examples and a cross-layer forecast-time comparison, but those findings do not directly measure stability or canonicality of SAE features.

untested.parts: All: no toy networks, no sparsity transition, no geometry.
All: no neuron polysemanticity and no capacity competition.
All: the subject is GraphCast (a weather GNN), not an LLM. Neuron-level distribution was not measured.
Completeness (no reconstruction-sufficiency or dark-matter analysis). Canonicality via cross-seed feature matching (none done). Sensitivity to dictionary size, sparsity or K.
All: feature dimensionality was not examined.

missing.what: Across all 16 layers × 5 seeds, the Top1–Top2 F1 gap and the correlation ordering within the Top 4 varied across seeds. This extends the R9-type seed-instability evidence beyond Layer 8.
In reference seed 50108, each layer's F1 leader had positive pressure-structure correlation (0.379–0.741) and ranked in the top two by correlation in 13/16 layers.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'challenges' label overstates the evidence. The paper never aligns or matches features across seeds. Its non-canonicality statements lean on cited work (Leask et al. 2025; Paulo & Belrose 2025), and its own data shows only variation in leader quality and roles. V5 applicability to a non-LLM weather model is assumed, since V5 does not restrict the system kind. Not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-network superposition, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Neuron polysemanticity and competition for limited capacity.
Polysemanticity arising for reasons other than capacity pressure.
The version concerns LLMs; this study examines GraphCast, an AI weather model.
Whether SAE features are complete descriptions of the representation; stability and canonicality beyond this model, phenomenon, and analysis.

rows.subject: GraphCast 0.25° checkpoint trained on ERA5
rows.operation_detail: Measured the dictionary-wide effective feature number for position correspondence (F1).
rows.measure: Dictionary-wide effective feature number for position F1
rows.note: Calculated across the 3,589 features with finite summaries for all three attribute measures. This indicates a distributed position relation in this dictionary, but does not establish completeness or canonicality.
rows.check: A single-SAE effective feature number for position F1. It measures how one attribute relation spreads across features, not SAE feature stability, completeness or canonicality.

rows.subject: GraphCast 0.25° checkpoint trained on ERA5
rows.operation_detail: Measured the dictionary-wide effective feature number for intensity D-proximity.
rows.measure: Dictionary-wide effective feature number for D-proximity
rows.note: The paper describes this relation as distributed much more broadly than position or pressure-structure correspondence.
rows.check: A single-SAE spread measure for D-proximity. It does not bear on whether SAE features are canonical or stable units.

rows.subject: GraphCast 0.25° checkpoint trained on ERA5
rows.operation_detail: Measured the dictionary-wide effective feature number for pressure-structure correlation.
rows.measure: Dictionary-wide effective feature number for pressure-structure correlation
rows.note: The paper describes this relation as distributed across a restricted but non-singleton subset of the dictionary.
rows.check: A single-SAE spread measure for pressure-structure correlation. It does not bear on V5.

rows.subject: GraphCast 0.25° checkpoint trained on ERA5
rows.operation_detail: Measured effective feature number for overlap between position F1 and pressure-structure relations.
rows.measure: Effective feature number of F1–pressure-structure overlap
rows.note: The overlap was more concentrated than either individual attribute distribution.
rows.check: A single-SAE overlap concentration measure. It does not bear on V5.

rows.subject: GraphCast 0.25° checkpoint trained on ERA5
rows.operation_detail: Measured effective feature participation among each independent Layer-8 SAE's F1-selected Top 4.
rows.measure: Effective feature number for position F1 within the Top 4
rows.note: The authors summarize this as position F1 being distributed across about 3–4 features.
rows.check: A within-Top-4 Neff across seeds. It shows the attribute-relation organization recurs, not that features match across fits. The Top-4 size was chosen exploratorily on seed 50108, and sensitivity to it was untested.

rows.subject: GraphCast 0.25° checkpoint trained on ERA5
rows.operation_detail: Measured effective feature participation among each independent Layer-8 SAE's F1-selected Top 4.
rows.measure: Effective feature number for D-proximity within the Top 4
rows.note: The authors summarize this as D-proximity being distributed across about 2–4 features.
rows.check: Same issue as R5: it measures organization recurrence, not feature stability.

rows.subject: GraphCast 0.25° checkpoint trained on ERA5
rows.operation_detail: Measured effective feature participation among each independent Layer-8 SAE's F1-selected Top 4.
rows.measure: Effective feature number for positive pressure-structure correlation within the Top 4
rows.note: Participation ranged from strong concentration to moderate distribution across about 1–3 features.
rows.check: Same issue as R5. The 'partial' state has no referent version.

rows.subject: GraphCast 0.25° checkpoint trained on ERA5
rows.operation_detail: Measured effective feature participation for the overlap between position F1 and pressure-structure relations among each independent Layer-8 SAE's F1-selected Top 4.
rows.measure: Effective feature number of F1–pressure-structure overlap within the Top 4
rows.note: Participation ranged from concentration in about one feature to moderate distribution across about 1–3 features.
rows.check: Same issue as R5. The 'partial' state has no referent version.

rows.subject: GraphCast 0.25° checkpoint trained on ERA5
rows.operation_detail: Compared the leading position feature and pressure-structure feature across independently trained Layer-8 SAEs.
rows.measure: Feature identity and leading-feature position F1 across fits
rows.value: Leading-feature median position F1 ranged from 0.345 to 0.512; its margin over the second-ranked feature ranged from 0.027 to 0.308. In seed 50112, the F1 leader was f277, while f3984 had the strongest pressure-structure correlation in the Top 4.
rows.note: The paper reports changing feature identity and ranking across decompositions, while the broader distributed but partially bundled organization recurred.
rows.check: Bears on stability. The leading feature's F1 and margin vary across seeds, and leader roles differ in seed 50112. Feature IDs are arbitrary across independent SAEs and no alignment was done, so 'different identity' is not itself a measured mismatch.

relationships.condition: Five independently seeded TopK SAEs (4,096 features, K=32) on GraphCast Layer-8 hidden states, cyclone readouts
relationships.reason: R9: the leading cyclone readout's quality (F1 0.345–0.512) and roles vary by seed, so single features are not stable across fits. Matching was not measured, so this is not a direct challenge.
relationships.display_finding: The leading cyclone readout's F1 ranged from 0.345 to 0.512 and its roles changed by seed, so single features were not stable across fits, though features were not matched across seeds.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Independent Layer-8 SAE decompositions of GraphCast cyclone states
reader_labels.reason: Feature identities and rankings vary across fits even though the broader attribute-relation organization recurs, challenging the claim that SAE features are stable canonical units in this setting (R5–R9). Completeness was not tested.
